Revit Skills Every BIM Architect Should Know

Modelling walls is the easy part. These are the Revit skills that make a BIM architect productive on a real multi-discipline project.

Almost every architect can build walls, floors and doors in Revit. What separates a productive BIM architect is the set of skills that keep a shared model healthy, documented and coordinated.

1. Worksharing

Working in a central model with worksets, borrowing elements correctly and syncing without overwriting colleagues. Mistakes here cost a whole team time.

2. Families

Understanding system, loadable and in-place families, building parametric loadable families with sensible parameters and keeping file size small. See our notes on Revit family creation.

3. View templates and graphics

Controlling graphics with view templates, filters and visibility settings rather than overriding view by view, so sheet sets stay consistent.

4. Documentation from the model

Producing plans, sections, elevations and details that are genuinely driven by the model, with schedules for doors, windows, rooms and finishes, rather than drafting over it.

5. Levels, grids and shared coordinates

Setting up and respecting levels, grids and shared coordinates so architectural, structural and MEP models align when federated.

6. Phasing and design options

Using phases for existing and new work and design options for alternatives, especially in refurbishment and fit-out.

7. Coordination

Linking consultant models, reviewing clashes in Navisworks or ACC and resolving openings, cores and ceiling zones with structure and MEP before issue.

8. Model health

Purging unused content, managing warnings, avoiding imported CAD in the model and auditing regularly.

9. Parameters and data

Using shared and project parameters correctly so data can be scheduled, checked and exported, including to IFC.

10. Basic automation

Knowing when a Dynamo script would save hours, even if a specialist writes it. See BIM automation.

These skills are part of what we test when assessing BIM architects for the ENGISOFT talent pool.
